svg.text: Four FAR dollar lines, and the bunching follows whichever one is in force
Each panel is one rule. Two lines per panel: the excess just below the old value and below the new one. Three of these thresholds moved in 2018.
anyone deciding whether below-threshold clustering is a rule
effect or a habit of round numbers
whether to screen on distance below the threshold in force that
a rule's excess stays at its old value after the line moved, or
the control rule moves with the others
a filled mark is the value that was the rule that year; a hollow one is the same value when it was not
excess awards just below, against the local trend
the one that runs backwards is the one that is not a behaviour at all
Below the micro-purchase line a purchase goes on a government card and is never filed as a contract action, so the register thins out under it instead of piling up. That is the same fact
figure 20 measures from the other side, where raising the line from $3,500 to $10,000 removed 78% of a missing fifth of a million awards. A rule can shape the distribution by changing
behaviour or by changing what gets written down, and only the first is worth screening for.
USAspending API v2 bulk download; FY2016, FY2017 and FY2025, eleven civilian departments, positive awards only. Threshold values and their change dates are the FAR's, not inferred.
Figure 12's estimator, imported unchanged. CAVEAT: a distribution tracking a rule is not evidence that any award was split, and none is identified. Defense (68.6% of federal contract
